lesson.title: The Sky Calendar
lesson.subtitle: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche — the Roman planetary week.

hook.title: Walking the Planetary Week From Moon to Sun
hook.content: The first five weekdays end in -di (Latin diēs 'day') after the Moon (lundi), Mars (mardi), Mercury (mercredi), Jupiter/Jove (jeudi), and Venus (vendredi). Then samedi puts -di at the end of Sabbath, and dimanche opens with di- (Dominica, the Lord's Day)!

footnotes.title: How to remember jeudi (Thursday) vs. mardi (Tuesday) and mercredi (Wednesday)
footnotes.content: Mercredi has three syllables like Wed-nes-day (both sit in the middle of the week); jeudi starts with J like Jupiter/Jove (the Roman Thor)!

pattern.title: lundi (On Monday) vs. le lundi (Every Monday)
pattern.content: Use the bare weekday for a single day (On se voit jeudi), and place le in front for a weekly routine (le lundi = 'every Monday').
pattern.linguist_note: Latin planetary week calqued Hellenistic astrological day names.
pattern.trap_note: Remember: never capitalize French weekdays in the middle of a sentence!

exercises.prompt: Match all seven French weekdays in calendar order:
exercises.target_answer: Monday & Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday & Sunday
exercises.meaning: lundi & mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi & dimanche
exercises.explanation: lundi through samedi end in -di; dimanche starts with di-.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'I arrive on Friday' vs. 'I work on Fridays (every Friday)'?
options: J'arrive sur vendredi / Je travaille chaque le vendredi
J'arrive vendredi / Je travaille le vendredi
J'arrive le vendredi / Je travaille vendredi
exercises.target_answer: J'arrive vendredi / Je travaille le vendredi
exercises.meaning: Bare weekday = this Friday; le + weekday = every Friday
exercises.explanation: le before a weekday turns a single day into a weekly habit.

exercises.prompt: Write the French weekday named after Jupiter/Jove ('Thursday'):

exercises.idea: we are going to the cinema on Saturday (use On va)
cues: We go to the cinema → On va au cinéma + Saturday → samedi
exercises.meaning: We're going to the cinema on Saturday
exercises.explanation: samedi stands bare at the end with no preposition.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Le dimanche, le restaurant est fermé
exercises.target_answer: Le dimanche, le restaurant est fermé
exercises.meaning: On Sundays, the restaurant is closed
exercises.affirmation: You used Le dimanche for the weekly schedule.

summary.outcome: Use all seven weekdays in single-event and habitual (le + weekday) schedules.

use_example.german: On se voit mercredi ou jeudi ?
use_example.english: Shall we see each other Wednesday or Thursday?

summary.takeaway: Five Roman gods + Sabbath + Lord's Day = the French week.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([1602] En janvier Gym): see how The Sky Calendar leads directly into En janvier Gym.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "We're going to the cinema on Saturday" in French:
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "On va au cinéma samedi" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of The Sky Calendar.

lundi.etymology_derivation: Moon-day, exactly like English Monday — both calendars still worship the moon.

mardi.etymology_derivation: Mars' day. English named Tuesday after Tiw, but mardi gras kept the Mars in the calendar.

jeudi.etymology_derivation: Jupiter's day — the Roman counterpart to Thor's Thursday.

vendredi.etymology_derivation: Venus's day — counterpart to Freya's Friday.

dimanche.etymology_derivation: Latin dies Dominica 'Day of the Lord'. Placing le before a weekday means 'every [weekday]'.

semaine.etymology_derivation: Latin septimāna, the seven-morning stretch. English had the same coin: sennight, seven nights — now extinct.
